page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 128 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are present on this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1873.78 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1456.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as indicated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3596.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2405.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% tier at 22.81 GB/sec and 12.89 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression is a strong point, reaching 32.63 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory capacity, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core performance. It is suited for basic web serving, lightweight single-threaded applications, and development or testing environments. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or multi-threaded processing due to its poor database operation benchmarks and weak multi-core scaling.
description: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is an x86_64 virtual server in the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 2 shared Intel vCPUs (1 physical core with hyper-threading), 4.0 GB of RAM, and 128 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1456.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.63 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are weak, with uncached large-block write speeds falling into the bottom 10% tier at 12.89 GB/sec, and database operations scoring poorly. Due to the shared CPU allocation and limited memory density, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic static web serving, and development environments rather than intensive database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or multi-threaded applications.
